parts.text:
"A weekend hackathon on scientific parallelism, about 30 hours, on 21 November. GPUs are provided; their type is not yet
known. Teams may bring their own problem, and the thinking, data and baseline can be prepared beforehand.

Judges score reshaping, a credible baseline, correctness and scientific value. A carefully explained failure to get a
speedup can still win, if its failure modes were predicted in advance.

The sponsors build systems that split workloads into subtasks and route each to the best chip, and low-latency
inference chips. The question they care about: which parts of a workload are sequential, and must they be?

Propose five projects for this hackathon, from any field of science. For each give: title; field; sequential_part, the part of the work that one answer waits on step after step, or \"none\"; restructure, how your project changes that (or what it runs in parallel); condition, what must hold for it to pay off; baselines, what the result is timed and checked against; first_test, the cheapest measurement to run first and its rough cost. Decide from what you know; do not use tools.

Return only one JSON value, with no other text, that matches this JSON Schema:
{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"proposals\"],\"properties\":{\"proposals\":{\"type\":\"array\",\"items\":{\"type\":\"object\",\"required\":[\"title\",\"field\",\"sequential_part\",\"restructure\",\"condition\",\"baselines\",\"first_test\"],\"properties\":{\"title\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"field\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"sequential_part\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"restructure\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"condition\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"baselines\":{\"type\":\"string\"},\"first_test\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}}}}"

We need answer JSON only. Need propose five projects hackathon scientific parallelism 30h Nov 21. Need schema. We need craft five objects with required fields. Need consider sponsors: systems split workloads into subtasks route each to best chip, low-latency inference chips. Question: which parts workload sequential, must they be? Need projects any field. Need each: title; field; sequential_part; restructure; condition; baselines; first_test. Need decide from knowledge.

Need produce one JSON value, no other text. Need be careful valid JSON. Let's generate five varied scientific projects, meaningful.

We need include sequential_part: part of work one answer waits on step after step, or "none". Restructure how project changes that (or what parallel). Condition what must hold for payoff. Baselines result timed and checked against. First_test cheapest measurement first and rough cost.

Let's think domains:
1) Molecular dynamics / protein folding: sequential part? MD time integration is sequential step after step due to force update and position update. Restructure: replication-based parallelism: run multiple replicas (ensembles), enhanced sampling, path-splitting, speculative parallel-in-time integration like parareal, or domain decomposition for forces? Hackathon could investigate which parts sequential: integration inherently sequential; forces parallel. Maybe "Multiple independent trajectories on GPUs, plus spatial domain decomposition within each time step; use asynchronous/ParaReal predictor-corrector across time." Condition: many independent replicas or long trajectories; force compute dominates; communication latency hidden. Baselines: single-GPU trajectory timings, OpenMM/GROMACS; accuracy vs sequential. First test: benchmark GROMACS/OpenMM on one GPU vs 4 GPU domain decomposition on small water box maybe $0 cloud? Provided GPUs, so cheap ~1 hour. Need roughness.

2) Bayesian inference MCMC: sequential part? MCMC chain is sequential: each sample depends on previous. Restructure: run multiple chains, parallel tempering, or subsampling / stochastic gradient, or embarrassingly parallel chains. Condition: chains can mix independently; target posterior parallel chains accepted; need enough memory. Baselines: single-chain ESS/sec, correctness vs posterior. First test: simple logistic regression with PyMC/NumPyro on CPU/GPU measuring effective sample size per second for 1 vs N chains, cost ~1 hour.

3) Phylogenetics / evolutionary tree search: sequential part? Tree search in maximum likelihood is iterative/sequential; likelihood computation per tree parallelizable. Restructure: parallel evaluate many candidate trees on GPUs (like BEAGLE/GPU) or run many starting trees across GPUs, parallel likelihood across sites and trees. Condition: independent site likelihoods or candidate evaluations; GPU arithmetic throughput pays off. Baselines: RAxML-NG/IQ-TREE 1 core / 1 GPU. First test: compute likelihood of small alignment on CPU vs GPU for fixed tree, cost minutes.

4) Weather/climate ensemble data assimilation: sequential part? assimilation cycles sequential (forecast then analysis then forecast), ensemble forecasts independent across members. Restructure: run ensemble members in parallel GPUs, maybe each member GPU; reduce sequential cycle by parallel-in-time assimilation? Could be too much. Condition: ensemble size large enough, model scaled to GPU. Baselines: single-member serial elapsed time. First test: run known toy model (Lorenz96) ensemble on CPU/GPU for e.g. 40 members vs sequential, cost ~1 hour.

5) Quantum chemistry: coupled cluster / many-body perturbation? sequential part: iterative solver (e.g. Davidson) sequential but tensor contractions parallel. Restructure: GPU tensor contractions, parallel over occupied/virtual indices, or parallel replica solve; maybe "quantum embedding/active space screening" etc. Condition: GPU memory / tensor core throughput. Baselines: PySCF/CPU tensor contractions vs GPU. First test: CCSD iteration on small molecule using cuQuantum or PySCF GPU, cost 1-2 hours.

Need maybe include one with sequential_part none? User says sequential_part the part... or "none". Could have one project with none (embarrassingly parallel). But perhaps question cares sequential parts. Maybe include one "none" project? Let's choose maybe one has "none" for project: e.g. high-throughput virtual screening/docking: each ligand independent, sequential_part none. Restructure: run ligand docking jobs across all GPUs; dynamic scheduling. Condition: lib docking throughput; scoring must be independent. Baselines: CPU single node docking with AutoDock Vina. First test: dock 100 ligands with Vina on CPU vs GPU/parallel across GPUs cost minutes-hours. Better include one none.

Need ensure each field is string. Need no markdown. Let's include five proposals.

Let's craft specific credible.

Proposal 1: Molecular dynamics with parallel-in-time and ensemble. Field "Computational biophysics". sequential_part: "The time integrator: each position/velocity update depends on the previous step's forces, so one trajectory advances step after step; forces within a step are parallel, but the stepping is serial." restructure: "Keep force decomposition across GPUs within each step, replicate many independent trajectories/ensembles across GPUs, and add a ParaReal-style coarse predictor-corrector to attempt parallel-in-time stepping; measure which layers (force, neighbor lists, communicator) dominate." condition: "Long trajectories or many replicas are needed; inter-step parallelization pays off only if force computation cost per step exceeds pinned communication latency and the coarse propagator is stable." baselines: "Single-GPU and single-node OpenMM/GROMACS trajectories; correctness against sequential order for energy, RMSD distributions and mean squared displacement." first_test: "Time 10 ns of a small solvated protein (about 25k atoms) with GROMACS/OpenMM on 1 vs 4 GPUs with domain decomposition; roughly 1 hour on provided hardware."

Proposal 2: MCMC maybe title "Parallel-chain Bayesian inference with GPU likelihood", field statistics/Bayesian inference. sequential_part: "A single Markov chain: the sample at step t is created from step t-1, so naive chain length cannot be parallelized." restructure: "Run many independent chains across GPUs, plus vectorized log-likelihood over particles; tune adaptively; use parallel tempering if mixing is poor." condition: "Target posterior has independent chain mixing; per-chain memory fits GPU; ESS/sec scales near linearly with chains; no excessive overhead for adaptation." baselines: "Single-chain No-U-Turn Sampler on CPU and GPU; compare effective sample size per second and posterior quantiles." first_test: "Fit a logistic regression / hierarchical model in NumPyro with 1 vs 8 chains on one GPU; roughly 1-2 hours."

Proposal 3: Docking with none. Title "GPU-accelerated high-throughput virtual screening". Field "Drug discovery / computational chemistry". sequential_part: "none" (each ligand scoring is independent). restructure: "Split the ligand library across all GPUs and CPU cores; batch docking poses inside each GPU; dynamic work-stealing load balancer; no sequential chain." condition: "Library size is large, scoring kernel occupancy is high, and inter-ligand independence holds (no shared state)." baselines: "AutoDock Vina / Gnina single workstation CPU and single GPU; compare screened ligands per hour and hit ranking." first_test: "Dock 100 ligands with Vina/Gnina on 1 CPU vs 1 GPU vs 4 GPUs and record punctual throughput; cost about 30-60 minutes."

Proposal 4: Phylogenetics. Title "Parallel likelihood evaluation for maximum-likelihood phylogenetics". Field "Evolutionary biology / phylogenetics". sequential_part: "Tree-search heuristics iterate: propose a tree rearrangement, evaluate its likelihood, and choose the next move; each serial search path depends on prior accepted moves." restructure: "Parallelize the inner likelihood over alignment sites and across many candidate trees/topologies on GPUs; run several independent searches and merge best trees to reduce the serial search path." condition: "GPU throughput on site likelihoods exceeds CPU and memory can hold conditional likelihood vectors; enough candidate moves to saturate all devices." baselines: "IQ-TREE/RAxML-NG single-core CPU and GPU; compare log-likelihood of final trees, elapsed search time, tree distance to reference." first_test: "Compute sitewise likelihoods for one fixed tree on a 1,000-taxon alignment on 1 CPU vs 1 GPU; cost minutes."

Proposal 5: Weather ensemble. Title "Parallel ensemble data assimilation with a toy atmospheric model". Field "Geophysics / numerical weather prediction". sequential_part: "The forecast-analysis cycle is sequential: each assimilation step needs the prior forecast, and the next forecast starts from that analysis." restructure: "Run all ensemble members concurrently on GPUs; within each member use GPU time-stepping; test whether parallelizing members hides the serial cycle and whether asynchronous ensemble filtering reduces wall-clock." condition: "Ensemble size is large enough or model on GPU fast enough; inter-member communication of covariance update remains cheap relative to member integration." baselines: "Serial single-member Lorenz96 with ensemble Kalman filter on CPU; compare analysis RMSE and wall-clock." first_test: "Run a 40-member Lorenz96 ensemble for 100 cycles on CPU vs one GPU vs multiple GPUs; about 1 hour."

Need consider "first_test" includes rough cost. all good.

Need output only JSON. Ensure no trailing commas. Use ASCII. Need maybe no newline? Fine. Let's craft final. Need valid JSON. Include field sequential_part "none" for docking.

Double-check schema requires no additional properties? It says properties define required. Additional properties? It may reject if extra? We only include required.

Let's ensure strings no unescaped quotes. Fine.

Need maybe include "baselines" mention timed and checked. Good.

Let's produce.
